title: Two rotors in series, one wired from a dictionary keyword strip and one hidden, in both orders
k4_result: 3,641,182,057,344 settings judged (through exact joins, 20 minutes for everything). 0 settings give a real hidden wiring with 7 or more forced coincidences. 1 setting passes with 5 (form A, KRYPTOS-numbered faces, strip AZTHIONIUM, fast word NOVEMBER, block 2 one on, slow start 20); its reading is gibberish (big-model score -6.45 per quadgram, word coverage 0.35; English needs -5.1). About one such chance pass at 5 coincidences is expected in a search this size.
controls: 3 shuffled K4s (KRYPTOS and the 84 theme strips in full, a different third of the dictionary strips each, about 1.2e12 settings each): 0 settings with 7+ coincidences, 0 with 5-6, nothing to read. K4's single 5-coincidence pass is not above this: it does not read as English.
planted: 6/6 (form A and form B, each with a constant speed, a 3-letter key and a theme word; random hidden wiring, random dictionary strip). Every planted setting was found and read back (58-75 of 97 letters, English score -3.9 to -4.6). In 5 of 6 the planted text was also the best reading of all survivors; for the form A 3-letter key 1,078 sister settings passed and one of them scored higher than the planted one.
scope_limits: Keyword rotor: KRYPTOS, 84 theme words and 220,232 dictionary keyword alphabets, as a strip read against A-Z both ways round; the strip against itself (1-25 places on) only for KRYPTOS and the theme words. No transposition-mixed alphabets. Fast turn (always the first rotor): 26 constant speeds, previous cipher letter, running sum of the cipher text, every key of length 1-3, 85 theme words plain and sliding (A-Z or KRYPTOS numbering); in form B with every start 0-25. Keys of length 4+ only if they are theme words. Slow turn (second rotor): constant inside each clue block with block 2 shifted 0-25, or one step per 26 letters at every offset; in form A with every start 0-25. In form A a step inside a clue block was tried only on KRYPTOS and the theme strips, and only for rules with a forced pair in the other block (all but 9-34 of 1,068 rules). Both rotors turn the same way; no reversed directions. Not judgeable at 7 coincidences on K4: 6-7% of form A fast rules (they were still tested at 5-6) and 2 of 48 form B slow shapes (also tested at 5). By random draws with K4's clue words, 68-100% of true settings reach 7 and 99-100% reach 5. Long turning keys that are not words, two hidden wirings (idea 82 form H), slow rotor first, three rotors and a reflector stay open.

negative.family: Two rotors in series, one keyword wiring and one hidden wiring
negative.hypothesis: K4 is two rotors in series, Y = R1[P+s]-s, C = R2[Y+t]-t, where one wiring is a dictionary keyword alphabet read as a strip and the other is hidden; the fast turn s is a speed, a short key or a theme word and the slow turn t is fixed inside each clue block or steps once per 26 letters.
negative.scope: 3.64e12 settings by an exact wire-collision test on the hidden rotor (no wiring guessed): 220,317 keyword alphabets as strips against A-Z both ways (KRYPTOS + 84 theme words also against themselves, 1-25 on); hidden rotor first or second; fast turn = 26 speeds, 2 cipher-fed rules, every key of length 1-3, 85 theme words plain and sliding; slow turn = block 2 shifted 0-25 or one step per 26 letters; A-Z/KRYPTOS faces; survivors completed and scored on the big English model.
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: K4 has 0 settings with 7+ forced coincidences and 1 with 5, which reads as gibberish (-6.45; English needs -5.1) (controls: 3 shuffled K4s, 0 with 5+; planted 6/6 found and read back; 68-100% of true settings reach 7 coincidences, 99-100% reach 5).

follow_ups: Same test with keys of length 4-6 for the fast turn. Form B is cheap (rules are looked up by their turn at two forced pairs, so 26^4-26^6 keys only cost index memory: split by key prefix). Form A needs the per-period trick: for period p the same-residue repeats of EASTNORTHEAST force equal middle letters whatever the key, which filters (strip, slow start) before any key is tried.

Keyword rotor made from the transposition-mixed keyword alphabets (kryptos.round11.mixes) and from the strip against itself for the whole dictionary (25 offsets): about 30 times this run's cost, so 2-3 hours, or restrict to the 22,000 common words.
Slow rotor first, fast rotor second (the hidden wiring on the slow rotor in front): the same engine with the two blocks' roles swapped; not covered here.
